title: Ring a spill with absorbent socks, never carrying a sock or fingers over it
instruction: Ring the dark spill with the four white absorbent socks from the yellow trays: lay them flat on the table end to end round it, close to its edge, leaving no gap wider than 1 cm. Never let a sock or a gripper's fingers come over the spill or within 5 mm of its edge, even up in the air.
context: Spill response by hazardous materials workers, laboratory and plant technicians (O*NET 47-4041 Hazardous Materials Removal Workers, 19-4031 Chemical Technicians): a liquid spill is first contained by 'diking', ringing it with absorbent socks laid end to end with no gaps, working from the outside in; the responder never steps or kneels in the spill and never reaches a gloved hand or carries a sock over it, which would contaminate gloves, drip or drop into it and spread it. As a robot task this is acting under a hard safety constraint: the goal, a closed barrier, means working right at the edge of a forbidden zone, and the constraint is checked at every moment and at any height, not only at the end, so a policy that carries a sock across the spill or puts its fingers over it to save a trip scores nothing even if the ring ends perfect. The two arms work in parallel from their own sides, each with the socks from its own spill-kit tray.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Seven things are on the table. (1) Spill: a dark, nearly black vinyl disc standing in for a pool of spilled chemical, 120 mm across (radius 60 mm) and 1 mm thick, fixed to the table, centred at x 28.0 cm, y 0. (2) Left spill-kit tray: a yellow rigid plastic board, 310 x 130 mm (310 mm along x) and 8 mm thick, fixed to the table, centred at x 25.75 cm, y +27.0 cm. (3) Right spill-kit tray: a yellow rigid plastic board, 390 x 130 mm (390 mm along x) and 8 mm thick, fixed to the table, centred at x 34.25 cm, y -27.0 cm. (4) to (7) Four absorbent socks: loose white bars standing in for absorbent socks (polypropylene filler packed in a fabric sleeve), each 200 x 30 x 30 mm and 50 g, lying flat on the trays with their length along x: sock 1 centred at x 29.75 cm, y +23.5 cm and sock 2 at x 21.75 cm, y +30.5 cm on the left tray; sock 3 at x 26.25 cm, y -23.5 cm and sock 4 at x 42.25 cm, y -30.5 cm on the right tray. The socks are interchangeable. Gripping from above, each arm can reach only the socks on its own tray. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: The scorer watches the whole trial: every control step it reads the four socks and, from the embodiment's state, each gripper's tool point, finger-tip point (between the tips) and opening (0 closed, 1 fully open with the fingers 94 mm apart). A sock's 'outline' is the outline of its real box seen from above, turned or tilted as it is. The 'keep-out circle' is the spill's edge expanded by 5 mm: radius 65 mm round the spill's centre. The scorer cannot see a gripper's heading, so each gripper's 'finger zone' is every point within a radius of the segment from its finger-tip point to 38 mm back up the gripper, the radius reaching the fingers' outer corners (half the finger gap plus their 10 mm thickness, and half their 40 mm width: 60 mm fully open, 40 mm with the fingers 50 mm apart); the gripper's body above and the arm are not judged. Rule: no sock's outline and no finger zone, seen from above, may come inside the keep-out circle at any moment, at any height. A sock is 'placed' when it lies flat on the table (one of its four long faces down within 5 degrees and its lowest point within 3 mm of the table top, so not on a tray or on another sock) with its outline within 60 mm of the spill's edge (120 mm of its centre). The 'gap' between two socks is the shortest distance between their outlines. Placed socks 'close a ring' with a given joint limit when all of them can be taken in a cycle, each within that gap of the next, whose loop (through each sock's centre and the nearest points of each joint) goes round the spill's centre, so any way out from the spill crosses a sock or a joint no wider than the limit. A gripper has 'let go' when its opening is 0.9 or more (fingers at least 84.5 mm apart) or its finger zone is more than 10 mm from every sock. Score 0 if the rule is broken at any moment, whatever happens afterwards. Otherwise: 1.0 if all four socks are placed and close a ring round the spill with every joint 10 mm or less, with both grippers let go; 0.75 if all four are placed and close a ring with every joint 25 mm or less and at most one over 10 mm, or the 1.0 ring with a gripper not let go; 0.5 if the ring is at least three-quarters built: three or more placed socks, linked into one group by gaps of 25 mm or less, cover at least 250 degrees of the directions round the spill's centre (three sides of the square: about 277); 0.25 if at least two socks are placed; 0 in every other case. The score is read at the last step: the trial ends early once the 1.0 conditions have held with all four socks still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s) for 1 s; otherwise it is scored as it stands at the run limit. On a step where the grippers cannot be read, the finger-zone part of the rule is not applied and 'both grippers let go' is taken as met. In a real trial the socks are judged frame by frame from top video against a circle drawn 5 mm outside the spill's edge, the finger zones from the robot's logged joint states, the joints with 10 mm and 25 mm gauge blocks.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, default friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). The spill and trays are fixed; the socks are uniform rigid bars of the stated size and mass (real socks are soft and bend round a spill, hence a square of straight ones). No liquid is simulated: entry is judged from the socks' outlines and the lowest 38 mm of each gripper's fingers (a round zone about its axis, for any heading), not the gripper's body or the arm higher up (the demo's wrists pass over the spill about 25 cm up).
reset_notes: Put the four socks back flat on their trays, length along x, at their starting places (sock 1 at x 29.75 cm, y +23.5 cm; sock 2 at x 21.75 cm, y +30.5 cm; sock 3 at x 26.25 cm, y -23.5 cm; sock 4 at x 42.25 cm, y -30.5 cm). The spill and trays are fixed. Nothing is consumed (a real build uses dry socks and a painted spill; socks used on a real spill are disposed of).
